verdicts.title: TRY003 was enabled in the same commit that introduced a 179-site idiom Ruff cannot see, so the new lint rule enforces nothing
verdicts.reasoning: Every link reproduced on the current tree. (1) pyproject.toml:248 has "TRY003" in [tool.ruff.lint].select and the ignore list (lines 261-267) does not contain it. (2) The comment block at pyproject.toml:215-223, headed 'Omitted only when they fight intentional design or are a separate documentation/typing project', still lists 'TRY003 - public semantic categories carry stable catch contracts without a bespoke exception class per diagnostic message' three lines above the select entry that enables it - a direct self-contradiction in the same file. (3) `git grep -E 'raise [A-Za-z_]+\(\*\(' -- packages` gives exactly 179 hits, all under packages/*/src (0 under any tests tree); at 4b13d82 the count was 0. (4) `git show 7b26f655 -- pyproject.toml` shows the same commit rewrote the TRY003 comment, added "TRY003" to select, and added it to both per-file-ignores ('**/tests/**' and 'tests/**' at pyproject.toml:299-300); that commit added 158 of the splat raise sites. (5) Ruff's behaviour verified in isolation: `ruff check --isolated --select TRY003` on `raise E(f"n_steps must be >= 1, got {n}")` reports TRY003 and exits 1, while the byte-identical message written as `raise E(*(f"n_steps must be >= 1, got {n}",))` reports 'All checks passed!' and exits 0. (6) `uv run ruff check --no-cache --select TRY003 packages/ tests/` on the current tree -> 'All checks passed!', exit 0. (7) `git show ff174f11` ('ci(auditing): restore the lint gate by fixing three TRY003 violations', PR #897) converts its three ValueError sites into ConfigurationError(*( ... ,)) rather than into message-carrying classes, confirming the splat is the codebase's sanctioned way to satisfy the rule. I looked for a reason this is benign and found none: nothing else in the repo (no test, no script) asserts anything about exception message placement, and the per-file-ignores confirm the rule is also off in every test tree. Severity stays low: this is lint-gate hygiene with no runtime, numerical, or privacy consequence - the splat is semantically identical to the plain call - so the only cost is a merge-gate rule pinned at zero violations plus 179 harder-to-read call sites. Not a duplicate of any open issue; the open CI umbrella #774 has all its children closed and none of them concern TRY003.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Established by direct reproduction, not hypothesis: pyproject.toml selects TRY003 while the codebase carries 179 raise sites (all in packages/*/src) written as `raise SomeError(*("message",))`, a form Ruff's TRY003 does not match, and TRY003 is additionally per-file-ignored for '**/tests/**' and 'tests/**'. `ruff check --select TRY003 packages/ tests/` therefore reports 'All checks passed!' on the current tree, and the same message written the plain way (`raise E(f"...")`) does fail the rule - verified with --isolated on a two-line file, exit 1 vs exit 0. A contributor who hits the rule and greps for precedent finds 179 examples of the splat workaround and copies it, so the merge-gate rule is structurally incapable of firing. PR #897 did exactly this for its three findings. The file also documents the opposite policy: the comment at pyproject.toml:215-223 lists TRY003 among rules 'omitted' with a rationale, three lines above the select entry enabling it. No runtime, numerical, or privacy effect; the cost is a dead lint gate, a contradictory config comment, and call sites that defeat a constructor arity check.

verdicts.title: The per-package wheel build inventory in build-distributions.yml has no coverage guard
verdicts.reasoning: Verified every link, and the inventory is complete today - this is a missing guard, not a live gap. (1) .github/workflows/build-distributions.yml:44-74 contains one `uv build . --wheel --out-dir dist` for the umbrella plus nine literal `uv build packages/opaque-<name> --wheel --out-dir dist` steps (base, engine, optimizers, dpsgd, dpftrl, auditing, patches, transformers, alignment); opaque-accounting is built by maturin in the separate build-native-artifacts job (:130-163). `ls packages/` returns exactly those ten directories, so all ten are currently covered (the finding's 'ten literal packages/opaque-* steps' is off by one - nine, plus the root). (2) No guard exists: `grep -rn 'build-distributions' .github tests` finds only workflow callers (ci.yml:174, pr.yml:343, prepare-release-implementation.yml:461) and WORKFLOWS.md; the only inventory guard in the repo is the 'Verify package test matrix' step at python-tests.yml:102-125 added by 6de5f9ca (PR #870), which awks its own file and comms against `find packages -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -type d -name tests`, i.e. it is scoped to the test matrix alone. (3) I read the downstream checks myself and neither closes the hole: check_wheel_internal_pins.py main() (lines 177-201) does `sorted(args.wheel_dir.glob('*.whl'))` and only validates the pins of wheels that exist; validate-distributions.yml's scenario asserts `len(opaque_versions) > 1` and that all installed opaque-* versions equal the umbrella version, neither of which is a completeness check. set_build_versions.sh does glob `packages/*/pyproject.toml`, but only to rewrite version pins - it never compares that set against what gets built. (4) The one genuine partial mitigation, which the finding itself names: validate-distributions installs `opaque[all]` with `--find-links dist --only-binary :all:`, and the root pyproject's extras (pyproject.toml:33-59) currently reach all ten distributions, so a new package wired into an `opaque` extra WOULD fail resolution there. The hole is therefore specifically a new standalone package that is not added to an `opaque` extra. (5) Scope check against tracking: issue #835 (OPQ-380) is closed as completed by PR #870, and its filed acceptance criteria concern python-tests.yml and the pyproject auto-pickup comment only - build-distributions.yml appears in the audit evidence line but not in the issue's criteria - so this is genuinely unaddressed rather than a reopened issue. Severity low and unchanged: latent process risk, zero current gap, no privacy or numerical consequence, and the fix is a ~10-line loop or comm guard.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Established: build-distributions.yml enumerates the wheels to build as nine hardcoded `uv build packages/opaque-<name>` steps plus the root, and nothing in the repository compares that list against `packages/*` (verified by reading check_wheel_internal_pins.py, validate-distributions.yml and set_build_versions.sh, and by grepping .github and tests for any such guard). All ten current packages are covered, so there is no gap today. The residual exposure is a future standalone package: the #870 guard forces the python-tests.yml edit, nothing forces the build-distributions.yml edit, and if the new package is not added to an `opaque[...]` extra then no wheel is built, validate-distributions still passes, and both the main dev-wheel publish and the release ship a set silently missing it. If the new package IS added to an `opaque` extra, validate-distributions fails at `uv pip install --find-links dist --only-binary :all: opaque[all]`, so the hole is confined to packages outside the umbrella bundle. Low severity, latent, CI-process only.

verdicts.title: The value-level CachedProcess.repeated_pld regression test was deleted one day after it landed, leaving only a mock with no real implementor
verdicts.reasoning: All factual links reproduced, including the mutation. (1) `git show 76fd4e3e --stat` (PR #885, 'test(accounting): cover cached repeated PLD forwarding', 2026-09-02) adds 29 lines to packages/opaque-accounting/tests/test_cached.py and 14 lines to packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_per_step.py; the latter is `test_cached_correlated_full_horizon_preserves_epsilon`, band_mf_strategy(bands=16), sample_rate=0.01, n_steps=128, asserting `(acc.cached(acc.per_step(proc)) * n).epsilon_at(delta) == (acc.per_step(proc) * n).epsilon_at(delta)` - exactly issue #834's first acceptance criterion. (2) `git log --diff-filter=D 4b13d82..12146ec4 -- .../test_per_step.py` -> 87404a1b, 'refactor(accounting)!: remove horizon prefix accounting (#894)', 2026-09-03. The whole file is gone and `acc.per_step` no longer exists anywhere in packages/*/src, so the deleted test could not have survived the refactor unchanged - the deletion is a consequence of a deliberate breaking API removal, not test-suite erosion, which the finding's framing understates. (3) `grep -rn 'def repeated_pld' packages/*/src` -> only _base.py:418 (the default) and composition/_cached.py:84 (the relay); no shipped process overrides it, so the relay cannot change any epsilon today. (4) The surviving test is the mock at test_cached.py:8-29, which patch.object's `repeated_pld` onto an `eps_delta` process. It passes (1 passed in 0.05s). (5) Mutation reproduced exactly as claimed: a pytest plugin deleting CachedProcess.repeated_pld, run over packages/opaque-accounting/tests + packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting + packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting under `-m 'not cuda and not mps and not slow and not distributed'`, gives '1 failed, 601 passed' and the single failure is test_cached_process_preserves_repeated_pld_override with 'assert 3.0 == 2.0'. So #834's SECOND acceptance criterion (the mutation must go red) still holds; what was lost is only the first (a value-level assertion on a correlated strategy), and it is now unconstructible because the API it used was removed. (6) _base.py:428-433 does still invite count-sensitive overrides, and the default is not a bare self_compose - it rescales mc_resolution per release - so a future MC-based override is a real possibility. Severity stays low: no current epsilon is affected, deletion of the relay is still caught, and the residual risk is entirely forward-looking. Not tracked as open: #834 is closed as completed by #885; this is a post-closure regression of one of its two criteria, so it is new rather than a duplicate.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Established: PR #885 added the value-level correlated-strategy epsilon assertion that issue #834 asked for, and PR #894 deleted it the next day by removing packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_per_step.py wholesale together with the `acc.per_step` API it exercised (a deliberate breaking refactor, so the test could not be kept as written). What remains is a single mock test that patches `repeated_pld` onto an eps_delta process. That mock still does its job: `del CachedProcess.repeated_pld` over the three accounting test trees gives 1 failed / 601 passed, reproduced here, and the one failure is that mock test - so removing the relay is still caught. No shipped process overrides `repeated_pld` (only _base.py:418's default and _cached.py:84's relay exist), so the relay is inert today and no reported epsilon is currently wrong or can silently change. The exposure is forward-looking only: the docstring at _base.py:428-433 still invites count-sensitive overrides, and if one lands there is no value-level test on a correlated strategy to catch a wrong-count or non-relaying cache - only a mock that stubs its own return value. Low severity, coverage-quality issue, no epsilon impact.

verdicts.title: allow-empty-test-selection still lets two distributed-lane legs report green on zero collected tests
verdicts.reasoning: Mechanically reproduced, but it is known and was explicitly declined. (1) .github/scripts/run_python_test_package.sh:43-46 is verbatim as claimed: on `status -eq 5 && ALLOW_EMPTY_TEST_SELECTION == true` it echoes a ::notice:: and exits 0, and the branch below it only records a result line when status != 5, so an empty step leaves no trace in TEST_RESULTS_FILE either. `git diff 4b13d82..12146ec4` on that script shows only the added `assert_cuda_available.sh` preflight call; the exit-5 path is untouched. (2) The flag is set on exactly the lanes claimed: pr.yml:81 (distributed), :145/:160/:177 (three CUDA lanes), ci.yml:41/:100/:112/:126, plus prepare-release-implementation.yml:314/398/415/434. (3) I read assert_cuda_available.sh and it does close the CUDA half properly - it keys on the marker expression (strips 'not cuda', then word-boundary-matches a positive `cuda`), and fails the lane unless torch reports a device AND arithmetic on a CUDA tensor reads back correctly. There is no equivalent for `distributed`. (4) I re-measured collection myself, one path at a time, `-m 'distributed and not cuda' --collect-only -q`, and got precisely the finding's numbers: opaque-base 0, opaque-accounting 0, opaque-auditing 0 (the whole Foundation leg), opaque-patches 0, tests 0 (the whole Integration leg); opaque-dpsgd 6/862, opaque-dpftrl 5/638, opaque-engine 10/667, opaque-optimizers 2/232, opaque-alignment 1/492, opaque-transformers 10/1049. So two of the five suite legs are green-on-zero on every run today, and if the `distributed` marker were renamed or dropped all five legs would exit 5 and all five would be converted to success while 'Python tests' - a `needs` of publish-dev-wheels at ci.yml:199-215 - stayed green. (5) The decisive caveat: I confirmed via the GitHub API that issue #836, 'Replace allow-empty-test-selection with a per-suite expected minimum', is closed with state_reason 'not_planned', closed by the repo owner on 2026-09-01, with zero comments and zero closing PRs. Its body states the same measured zeros and the same acceptance criteria this finding proposes. The maintainer therefore reviewed this exact proposal and declined it without a code change. Its parent umbrella #774 ('Close CI fail-open gates and restore test integrity') is still OPEN, so I am marking this already_tracked=774: the substance is tracked work under an open umbrella whose specific child was deliberately rejected, and it should be filed as known-and-declined rather than as a new finding. Severity low: CI-gate hygiene, no privacy or numerical consequence, and it requires a second, separate mistake (losing the marker) to actually hide a regression.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Established by re-measurement: run_python_test_package.sh:43-46 converts pytest's exit 5 ('no tests collected') to success whenever ALLOW_EMPTY_TEST_SELECTION is true, which is set on the distributed lane and the three CUDA lanes in both pr.yml and ci.yml. Under the distributed lane's exact marker `distributed and not cuda`, two of the five suite legs collect zero tests today - Foundation (opaque-base 0, opaque-accounting 0, opaque-auditing 0) and Integration tests (tests 0), plus opaque-patches 0 inside an otherwise non-empty leg - so those legs' green checks carry no information. The CUDA half of the original exposure is genuinely closed: assert_cuda_available.sh keys on the marker expression and fails a cuda-selecting lane unless a CUDA tensor computes correctly. There is no analogous assertion for `distributed`, so if that marker were renamed, removed, or the spawn tests moved, all five legs would exit 5, all five would convert to success, and 'Python tests' - a needs of publish-dev-wheels - would go green having run no distributed test. That requires a second mistake to bite; nothing is silently broken now. Known and declined: issue #836 proposed exactly this fix (per-suite MIN_TESTS or a per-lane nonzero-total assertion) and was closed not_planned by the maintainer with no code change; its parent #774 remains open.
